processing: Mostly steamed sencha, as is usual for Kagoshima: leaves are steamed, rolled and dried, then finished by the tea maker. Steaming length varies by producer.
harvest_season: Spring first flush is the prized picking, as with other Japanese sencha; exact dates vary with altitude and producer.
appearance_dry: Typical of sencha: fine, dark green needles, with some variation between producers.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, as is typical of a lightly steamed sencha.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf pieces, like other sencha.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about a single Kirishima taste; expect the usual sencha balance of fresh vegetal aroma, savoury depth and a mild astringent finish.

brewing.notes: General sencha advice: cool the water, use a small pot, and pour out every drop between steeps.

vintage_note: Sold like other Japanese green tea, by the current year's harvest, with new-crop shincha appearing in spring. It is meant to be drunk fresh, not aged, so check the packing date and the flush.
description:
Kirishima-cha is the green tea of Kirishima city in Kagoshima, grown around the foot of the Kirishima mountains in the middle of the prefecture. Kagoshima is one of Japan's largest tea regions, and Kirishima is among its bigger producing areas.

Growers credit the place: cool mornings and evenings, and mist that softens the sun on the bushes. That is a common claim for Japanese mountain tea, and here it comes with real terrain, with Takachiho-no-mine and Karakuni-dake rising to the north.

There is no single house style to memorise. Treat it as sencha: moderate heat, a small pot, a short second steep. Too-hot water brings out bitterness and hides the sweetness you paid for.

Buy by producer and flush, since the regional name covers a range of quality. Mizobe-cha, from the Jusantsukabaru plateau within the city, is the local name to try next.
history:
Local accounts give the area a long tea history, including a story of a large old tea tree dated to around 1320; treat that as tradition, as little firm documentation is easy to find.

The modern reputation is better attested: Kirishima is reported to have taken the production-area prize for ordinary sencha at the national tea fair in 2017, 2018 and 2019.
